edges.label: Battelle co-operates ORNL through UT-Battelle, LLC
edges.note: Contract DEAC0500OR22725, recorded at approximately $42.3 billion, running 1999-2030.

edges.label: MITRE founding site and original headquarters
edges.note: Bedford, Massachusetts is the other of MITRE's two principal locations, at 202 Burlington Road. No MITRE-administered FFRDC is registered at Bedford on the NSF master list, so unlike McLean the Bedford tie is corporate rather than FFRDC-contractual.

edges.label: Battelle Memorial Institute headquarters
edges.note: Battelle Memorial Institute's own IRS Form 990 filings give its address as Columbus, Ohio. The FFRDCs it administers or co-administers sit at Idaho Falls, Richland and Aiken, none of them at Columbus, so the Columbus tie is the institute's own seat rather than a federal laboratory site.

edges.label: Operates the only FFRDC sponsored by the National Security Agency
edges.note: IDA's Center for Communications and Computing is sponsored by NSA/CSS - the least publicly visible FFRDC in the country and the hardest for a committee to reach.

a.label: Johns Hopkins University Applied Physics Laboratory

edges.label: A UARC, not an FFRDC - the unexamined branch of the same mechanism
edges.note: University Affiliated Research Centers carry FFRDC-like access without the FAR 35.017 sponsoring-agreement regime or NSF master-list registration; no congressional UAP letter has gone to one.

edges.label: MITRE McLean headquarters campus
edges.note: MITRE names McLean, Virginia as one of its two principal locations, with four buildings on Colshire Drive. McLean is where the defence and intelligence FFRDC work sits: the NSF master list registers the National Security Engineering Center, the Center for Advanced Aviation System Development, the Center for Enterprise Modernization and HSSEDI at McLean.

edges.label: RAND invented the institutional form the whole domain rests on
edges.note: Incorporated 1948 out of Project RAND inside Douglas Aircraft; now operates four FFRDCs for the Air Force, Army, OSD and DHS.

edges.label: RAND headquarters since its 1948 formation
edges.note: The NSF master list registers Project AIR FORCE, the Arroyo Center and the National Defense Research Institute at Santa Monica, California - three of RAND's four FFRDCs, the fourth being the Homeland Security Operational Analysis Center at Arlington, Virginia. This is where the contractor-operated analytical institution was invented.

edges.label: the FFRDC seam is a species of contracting mechanics, not a separate subject
edges.note: FAR 35.017 is a procurement regulation. The records status, disclosure direction and sole-source features that make the FFRDC form load-bearing on this board are all properties of the contracting instrument, which is why the seam domain should hang off contracting mechanics rather than float beside it.

edges.label: the largest operator of the one acquisition form built to be non-competitive by design
edges.note: MITRE operates multiple FFRDCs. FAR 35.017 permits an agency to meet special long-term research needs through a sponsoring agreement with a single operator outside full and open competition, and obliges the FFRDC to disclose its activities to its sponsor and to no one else. That is a contracting mechanism, and MITRE is its largest single instance.

b.label: Homeland Security Systems Engineering and Development Institute (HSSEDI)

edges.label: MITRE operates HSSEDI for DHS Science and Technology
edges.note: Created 5 March 2009; the DHS engineering franchise sits with the same operator now under congressional UAP records demand.

edges.label: MITRE is the largest single operator of the FFRDC form
edges.note: MITRE operates six of the 41 FFRDCs recorded by NSF, spanning defence/intelligence, aviation, tax, health, homeland security and cybersecurity sponsors - the widest sponsor spread of any operator.
